title: Chapter 4. Gaura's Form, Navadvipa, the Sannyasa and the Return
html:
Padas of contemporaries which Majumdar (*Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan, ch. 2) regards as eyewitness testimony, in the order of the lilas: the six-armed form and the beauty of Gorachand in Navadvipa, Radha's mood in Gadadhara's lap, the swing festival on the bank of the Ganga, the goshtha-lila, praise of Gaura and Nityananda; then Vasu Ghosha's cycle on the sannyasa (the last night at home, the lament of Shachi and Vishnupriya, Katwa, Keshava Bharati, the shorn curls, the lament of Nadia), the dance of the Lord as a sannyasi, and the Lord's return to the neighbourhood of Navadvipa (1514/15). The text follows the Padakalpataru (PK), the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR), the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC) and the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

1. Ananta Dasa — "kām̐cā se soṇāra tanu…" (PK 2167)

Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord's six-armed form (shad-bhuja): Rama's bow and arrows, Krishna's flute, the sannyasi's staff and waterpot. In PK the pada is headed "Then the form that revealed six arms, in Navadvipa". Majumdar mentions this pada when speaking of Ananta Dasa, a poet of Advaita's branch and a contemporary of the Lord. Raga tirotha-dhanashi.1

কাঁচা সে সোণার তনু ডগমগি অঙ্গ ।
চাঁদ-বদনে হাসি অমিয়া-তরঙ্গ ॥

kām̐cā se soṇāra tanu ḍagamagi aṅga |
cām̐da-badane hāsi amiyā-taraṅga ||

kancha se sonara tanu — a body like pure gold; dagamagi anga — the whole body quivering (glowing); chanda-badane — on the moon-face; hasi — a smile; amiya-taranga — waves of nectar

1.1His body is like pure gold, all of it quivering;
on His moon-face a smile — waves of nectar.

অবনি-বিলম্বিত বনি বনমাল ।
সৌরভে বেঢ়ল মধুকর-জাল ॥

abani-bilambita bani banamāla |
saurabhe beṛhala madhukara-jāla ||

abani-bilambita — hanging down to the earth; bani banamala — a lovely forest garland; saurabhe — by the fragrance; bedhala — surrounded; madhukara-jala — swarms of bees

1.2A forest garland hangs down to the very earth;
drawn by its fragrance, swarms of bees surround it.

উত ছয় ভুজ পর খর শর-চাপ ।
হেরইতে রিপুগণ থরহরি কাঁপ ॥

uta chaya bhuja para khara śara-cāpa |
heraite ripugaṇa tharahari kām̐pa ||

uta — there (?); chhaya bhuja para — upon the six arms (on the [upper] of the six arms); khara shara-chapa — sharp arrows and a bow; heraite — on seeing; ripugana — the enemies; tharahari kapa — tremble and shake

1.3Of the six arms the upper ones hold sharp arrows and a bow —
at the sight of them enemies tremble.2

দুরবা-দল-তুল নখ-বিধু সাজ ।
মণিময় কঙ্কণ বলয় বিরাজ ॥

durabā-dala-tula nakha-bidhu sāja |
maṇimaya kaṅkaṇa balaya birāja ||

duraba-dala-tula — like blades of durva grass; nakha-bidhu saj — moon-like nails adorn [them]; manimaya kankana balaya — jewelled bracelets and armlets; biraj — shine

1.4These arms are the colour of durva grass, their nails like moons;
bracelets and armlets of jewels shine on them.

তদধহিঁ দুহুঁ কর জলধর-শ্যাম ।
তহিঁ শোভে মোহন মুরলি অনুপাম ॥

tadadhahim̐ duhum̐ kara jaladhara-śyāma |
tahim̐ śobhe mohana murali anupāma ||

tadadhahi — below them; duhu kara — two hands; jaladhara-shyama — dark as a rain-cloud; tahi — in them; shobhe — shines; mohana murali — the enchanting flute; anupama — matchless

1.5Below, two arms dark as a thundercloud;
in them gleams the matchless, enchanting flute.

নখ-মণি বিধু জিনি তলহি সুরঙ্গ ।
মণি-অভরণ তাহে মুরছে অনঙ্গ ॥

nakha-maṇi bidhu jini talahi suraṅga |
maṇi-abharaṇa tāhe murache anaṅga ||

nakha-mani — the jewel-nails; bidhu jini — outshine the moon; talahi suranga — the palms are red; mani-abharana tahe — the jewelled ornaments on them; murachhe ananga — Ananga (Kamadeva) swoons

1.6The jewel-nails outshine the moon, the palms are red;
seeing the jewelled ornaments on them, Ananga himself swoons.3

তদধহি করহি কমণ্ডলু দণ্ড ।
যাহে কলি-কলমষ পাষণ্ড খণ্ড ॥

tadadhahi karahi kamaṇḍalu daṇḍa |
yāhe kali-kalamaṣa pāṣaṇḍa khaṇḍa ||

tadadhahi — lower still; karahi — in the hands; kamandalu danda — the waterpot and staff; yahe — by which; kali-kalamasha — the filth of Kali; pashanda — the godless; khanda — are shattered

1.7Lower still, hands with the waterpot and the staff,
which shatter the filth of Kali and the godless.4

গিম সঞে উরে মণি মোতি বিলোল ।
শ্রীবৎসাঙ্কিত কৌস্তভ দোল ॥

gima sañe ure maṇi moti bilola |
śrībatsāṅkita kaustabha dola ||

gima sanye ure — at the throat and on the breast; mani moti bilola — jewels and pearls sway; shribatsankita — [the breast] marked with the Shrivatsa; kaustubha dola — the Kaustubha swings

1.8At the throat and on the breast jewels and pearls sway;
the Kaustubha swings, the breast is marked with the Shrivatsa.

মলয়জময় উর পরিসর পীন ।
নাভি গভির কটি কেশরি-খীণ ॥

malayajamaya ura parisara pīna |
nābhi gabhira kaṭi keśari-khīṇa ||

malayajamaya — anointed with sandal; ura parisara pina — the broad, full chest; nabhi gabhira — the navel deep; kati keshari-khina — the waist slender as a lion's

1.9The broad chest is anointed with sandal;
the navel is deep, the waist slender as a lion's.

বসন সুরঙ্গ চরণ-পরিযন্ত ।
পদ-নখ-নীছনি দাস অনন্ত ॥

basana suraṅga caraṇa-pariyanta |
pada-nakha-nīchani dāsa ananta ||

basana suranga — the red cloth; charana-pariyanta — down to the feet; pada-nakha-nichhani — self-offering to the toenails; dasa ananta — Ananta Dasa

1.10The red cloth falls to His very feet;
Ananta Dasa offers himself to the nails of His feet.5

vol. 3, PDF p. 256, printed p. 245; MS P-R-Sa no. 2274); in GPT1 — p. 141, no. 89; in GPT2 — sect. 3.1, twice (nos. 44 and 89), with minor variants. The Lord revealed the six-armed form to Nityananda in Navadvipa (CB Madhya 5; Murari 2.8) and to Sarvabhauma in Puri (CC Madhya 6). Majumdar regards Ananta Dasa as a contemporary; PK has 32 padas with his signature. body. PK reads "uta chaya bhuja para" ("there, of the six arms…"), GPT "ubhadvaya bhujapara" ("on the two raised arms"); the sense is the same. the god of love. For "the godless" (pāṣaṇḍa) MSS "ka", "ca" read "filth" (kaluṣa); so also GPT: "the filth, the sin of Kali". away; the poet "offers himself" in such an offering to the nails of the Lord's feet. MSS "ka", "ca", P-R-Sa read "nichani".

2. Govinda Ghosha — "gorācām̐da kibā tomāra badana-maṇḍala…" (PK 1029)

Lila: Gorachand's form — a song of the Lord's beauty in Navadvipa. In PK it opens the section "Delight in the form" (rupa-ullasa) as a gaura-chandrika. According to Majumdar, Govinda Ghosha, the eldest of the Ghosha brothers, conveys his own impression of Gauranga's form. Raga dhanashi.6

গোরাচাঁদ কিবা তোমার বদন-মণ্ডল ।
কনক-কমল কিয়ে শরদ-পূর্ণিমা-শশী
নিশি দিশি করে ঝলমল ॥ ধ্রু ॥

gorācām̐da kibā tomāra badana-maṇḍala |
kanaka-kamala kiye śarada-pūrṇimā-śaśī
niśi diśi kare jhalamala || dhru ||

gorachand — Gorachand; kiba — how wondrous; tomara badana-mandala — the orb of Your face; kanaka-kamala — a golden lotus; kiye — or; sharada-purnima-shashi — the full autumn moon; nishi dishi — night and day; kare jhalamala — shines

2.1(Refrain) Gorachand, how wondrous is the orb of Your face!
Is it a golden lotus, is it the full autumn moon —
it shines by night and by day.

তোমার বরণখানি জনু হরিতাল জিনি
কিয়ে থির বিজুরী জিনিয়া ।
কিয়ে নব গোরোচনা কিয়ে দশবান সোণা
মনমথ-মন-মোহনিয়া ॥

tomāra baraṇakhāni janu haritāla jini
kiye thira bijurī jiniyā |
kiye naba gorocanā kiye daśabāna soṇā
manamatha-mana-mohaniyā ||

tomara barana-khani — the colour of Your body; janu — as if; haritala jini — surpassing orpiment; kiye thira bijuri jiniya — or surpassing a motionless lightning; kiye naba gorochana — is it fresh gorochana; kiye dashabana sona — is it gold of the finest assay; manamatha-mana-mohaniya — enchanting the mind of Manmatha

2.2The colour of Your body outshines yellow haritala
and seems to surpass a motionless lightning;
is it fresh gorochana, is it gold of the finest assay —
You enchant the mind of Manmatha himself.7

খগপতি জিনি নাসা অমিয়া-মধুর ভাষা
তুলনা না হয় ত্রিভুবনে ।
আকর্ণ নয়ান-বাণ ভুরু-ধনু-সন্ধান
কটাক্ষে হানয়ে নারী-মনে ॥

khagapati jini nāsā amiyā-madhura bhāṣā
tulanā nā haya tribhubane |
ākarṇa nayāna-bāṇa bhuru-dhanu-sandhāna
kaṭākṣe hānaye nārī-mane ||

khagapati jini nasa — a nose surpassing [the beak of] the king of birds (Garuda); amiya-madhura bhasha — speech sweet as nectar; tulana na haya tribhubane — no comparison in the three worlds; akarna nayana-bana — eyes reaching to the ears are arrows; bhuru-dhanu-sandhana — brows a drawn bow; katakshe hanaye — pierces with sidelong glances; nari-mane — the hearts of women

2.3Your nose is lovelier than Garuda's beak, Your speech sweet as nectar —
there is none like You in the three worlds.
Eyes reaching to the ears are arrows, brows a drawn bow:
with a sidelong glance You pierce the hearts of women.8

আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ বিলেপিত মলয়জ
অঙ্গুরী বলয়া তাহে সাজে ।
সিংহ জিনি মধ্য সরু হেম-রম্ভা জিনি উরু
চরণে নূপুর বঙ্করাজে ॥

ājānulambita bhuja bilepita malayaja
aṅgurī balayā tāhe sāje |
siṃha jini madhya saru hema-rambhā jini uru
caraṇe nūpura baṅkarāje ||

ajanulambita bhuja — arms reaching to the knees; bilepita malayaja — anointed with sandal; anguri balaya — rings and bracelets; tahe saje — shine on them; simha jini madhya saru — a waist slenderer than a lion's; hema-rambha jini uru — thighs surpassing golden plantain stems; charane nupura bankaraje — on the feet, anklets (bankaraj)

2.4Arms reaching to the knees are anointed with sandal,
and rings and bracelets shine on them.
The waist is slenderer than a lion's, the thighs like golden plantain stems,
on the feet are anklets.

জিনি ময়মত্ত হাতী হংসরাজ জিনি গতি
দেখিয়ে এ হেন রূপ-রাশি ।
কহয়ে গোবিন্দ ঘোষ গোর মনে সন্তোষ
নিছনি যাইয়ে হেন বাসি ॥

jini mayamatta hātī haṃsarāja jini gati
dekhiye e hena rūpa-rāśi |
kahaye gobinda ghoṣa gora mane santoṣa
nichani yāiye hena bāsi ||

jini mayamatta hati — surpassing a maddened elephant; hamsaraj jini gati — a gait surpassing the king of swans; dekhiye — seeing; e hena rupa-rashi — such a treasury of beauty; kahaye gobinda ghosha — Govinda Ghosha says; gora mane santosha — with joy at heart for Gora (?); nichhani yaiye — I would offer myself up; hena basi — so I feel

2.5The gait is lovelier than a maddened elephant's and the king of swans';
seeing such a treasury of beauty,
Govinda Ghosha speaks, with joy in his heart for Gora:
"I would give myself up for Him."9

under the heading "Now, delight in the form. Sri Gaurachandra" and opens the songs on the beauty of Radha and Krishna. It is not in GPT. Majumdar names PK 1029 and 2146 (no. 3) among Govinda Ghosha's padas on Gaura's form. (daśabān) is gold refined many times, of the finest assay. Manmatha is Kamadeva: the Lord's beauty enchants the god of love himself (cf. Krishna's name Madana-mohana). MS P-R-Sa reads "tanu" ("body") for "janu" ("as if"). of describing beauty; we translate faithfully. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never looked at another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). "Give myself up" (nichani jāiye) — see note 5. For "maddened" (mayamatta) MSS "ka", "kha" read "madamatta" (same sense).

3. Govinda Ghosha — "kanayā kaṣila mukha-śobhā…" (PK 2146)

Lila: Gaura's form — the causeless smile, the yellow silk, a bee flying to His feet. According to Majumdar, an eyewitness's impression of Gauranga's form. Raga sindhura.10

কনয়া কষিল মুখ-শোভা ।
হেরইতে জগ-মন লোভা ॥

kanayā kaṣila mukha-śobhā |
heraite jaga-mana lobhā ||

kanaya kashila — gold tried on the touchstone; mukha-shobha — the beauty of the face; heraite — on seeing; jaga-mana lobha — the mind of the world longs

3.1The beauty of His face is like gold tried on the touchstone;
one glance, and the mind of the whole world is filled with longing.

বিনি হাসে গোরা-মুখ হাস ।
পরিধান পীত পটবাস ॥

bini hāse gorā-mukha hāsa |
paridhāna pīta paṭabāsa ||

bini hase — smiles without cause; gora-mukha hasa — Gora's face, the smile; paridhana — wearing; pita patabasa — yellow silk garments

3.2Without any cause Gora's face smiles;
He is clad in yellow silk.11

অঙ্গের সৌরভ-লোভ পাইয়া ।
নবীন ভ্রমরী আইল ধাইয়া ॥

aṅgera saurabha-lobha pāiyā |
nabīna bhramarī āila dhāiyā ||

angera saurabha-lobha paiya — drawn by the fragrance of the body; nabina bhramari — a young bee; aila dhaiya — came flying

3.3Drawn by the fragrance of His body,
a young bee has come flying;

ঘুরি ঘুরি বুলে পদ-তলে ।
গুণ গুণ শবদ রসালে ॥

ghuri ghuri bule pada-tale |
guṇa guṇa śabada rasāle ||

ghuri ghuri bule — circles round and round; pada-tale — at the feet; guna guna shabada — a humming sound; rasale — sweet

3.4round and round it circles at His feet,
humming sweetly.

গোবিন্দ ঘোষের মনে জাগে ।
গোরা না দেখিলে বিষ লাগে ॥

gobinda ghoṣera mane jāge |
gorā nā dekhile biṣa lāge ||

gobinda ghoshera mane jage — in Govinda Ghosha's heart it awakens; gora na dekhile — if I do not see Gora; bisha lage — [all] tastes of poison

3.5In Govinda Ghosha's heart it awakens:
if I do not see Gora, everything tastes of poison.

p. 237; MS P-R-Sa no. 2253); GPT1 — p. 116, no. 17; GPT2 — sect. 3.1, no. 17 (almost without variants). Majumdar quotes from it the lines "without cause Gora's face smiles" and "if I do not see Gora, everything tastes of poison". Krishna's garment; in Navadvipa the Lord, in Krishna's mood, asked for yellow cloth (cf. PK 2122, chapter 3, no. 1). MS P-R-Sa: "mukhe" ("on the face").

4. Govinda Ghosha — "śrīdāma sudāma saṅge ye rasa karilum̐ raṅge…" (PK 2128; BR, p. 919)

Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord remembers the pastimes of Vrindavana and, crying "The flute, the flute!", falls senseless into Gadadhara's lap; then, in Radha's mood, He repeats Her name and calls Lalita and Vishakha. Around Him are Vasu Ghosha, Ramananda, Srivasa, Jagadananda, Narahari. According to Majumdar — an eyewitness's testimony; he cites the line about Narahari as proof that Narahari Sarakara was with the Lord already in Navadvipa. Raga mangala (PK, GPT), dhanashi (BR).12

শ্রীদাম সুদাম সঙ্গে যে রস করিলুঁ রঙ্গে
বলি পহু করে উতরোল ।
মুরলী মুরলী করি মুরছিত গৌরহরি
পড়ে পহু গদাধর-কোল ॥

śrīdāma sudāma saṅge ye rasa karilum̐ raṅge
bali pahu kare utarola |
muralī muralī kari murachita gaurahari
paṛe pahu gadādhara-kola ||

shridama sudama sange — with Shridama and Sudama; ye rasa karilu range — the pastimes (rasa) I enjoyed with delight; boli — saying; pahu kare utarola — the Lord cries out in agitation; murali murali kari — crying "the flute, the flute"; murachhita gaurahari — Gaurahari swoons; pare pahu gadadhara-kola — the Lord falls into Gadadhara's lap

4.1"The pastimes I enjoyed so gladly with Shridama and Sudama!.." —
saying this, the Lord cries out in agitation.
Crying "The flute, the flute!", Gaurahari loses consciousness,
and the Lord falls into Gadadhara's lap.13

রাস-রস বৃন্দাবন প্রিয় সখা সখীগণ
উপজয়ে প্রেম-তরঙ্গ ।
বাসুঘোষ রামানন্দ শ্রীবাস জগদানন্দ
মাতে পহু নরহরি সঙ্গ ॥

rāsa-rasa bṛndābana priya sakhā sakhīgaṇa
upajaye prema-taraṅga |
bāsughoṣa rāmānanda śrībāsa jagadānanda
māte pahu narahari saṅga ||

rasa-rasa — the rasa-lila; vrindavana — Vrindavana; priya sakha sakhigana — dear friends and girl-companions; upajaye prema-taranga — waves of prema arise; basughosha ramananda shribasa jagadananda — Vasu Ghosha, Ramananda, Srivasa, Jagadananda; mate pahu — the Lord is intoxicated; narahari sanga — together with Narahari

4.2The rasa-lila, Vrindavana, the dear friends and girl-companions —
waves of prema rise.
Vasu Ghosha, Ramananda, Srivasa, Jagadananda —
with Narahari the Lord is intoxicated.14

রাধা-ভাবে বিভোরা বরণ হইল গোরা
রাধা নাম জপে অনুক্ষণ ।
ললিতা বিশাখা বলি পহু যান গড়াগড়ি
কাহাঁ মোর গিরি গোবর্দ্ধন ॥

rādhā-bhābe bibhorā baraṇa haila gorā
rādhā nāma jape anukṣaṇa |
lalitā biśākhā bali pahu yāna gaṛāgaṛi
kāhām̐ mora giri gobarddhana ||

radha-bhabe bibhora — absorbed in Radha's mood; barana haila gora — the complexion became golden; radha nama jape anukshana — ceaselessly repeats Radha's name; lalita vishakha boli — crying "Lalita, Vishakha"; pahu yana garagari — the Lord rolls on the ground; kaha mora giri gobardhana — where is My hill Govardhana

4.3Absorbed in Radha's mood, He has become golden — Gora —
and ceaselessly repeats Radha's name.
Crying "Lalita, Vishakha!", the Lord rolls on the ground:
"Where is My hill Govardhana?

কাহাঁ যমুনার তট কাহাঁ মোর বংশীবট
বলি পুন হরল চেতন ।
এ দীন গোবিন্দ ঘোষে তা পাওল লব-লেশে
ধিক রহু ঐছন জীবন ॥

kāhām̐ yamunāra taṭa kāhām̐ mora baṃśībaṭa
bali puna harala cetana |
